page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor operates at a base speed of 2.2 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. This instance does not include any bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the e2-highmem-2 sits in the lower performance tiers. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is weak, scoring 1101.98, while multi-core performance drops into the bottom 10% with a score of 1451.88. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers measured at 12.0 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 10.51 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show similar limitations, with a passmark CPU encryption score of 2114.68 and single-threaded gzip compression at 18.76 GB/sec.

Given the high memory allocation relative to its processing power, this instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high computational throughput. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, caching layers, and lightweight web serving, though its static web serving throughput is limited to 1.43 GB/sec. The primary tradeoff is the low processing and memory bandwidth performance, making it unsuitable for heavy compute, large-scale data compilation, or complex LLM inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance equipped with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, it features 1 physical core with hyper-threading and a 16 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data positions this server in the lower performance brackets, with a single-core stress-ng score of 1101.98 and a multi-core score of 1451.88. Memory bandwidth is limited, reaching 12.0 GB/sec for large block reads. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core alongside modest processing capabilities, the e2-highmem-2 is best suited for lightweight, memory-dependent applications such as small databases, basic caching, and low-traffic web serving where resource density is prioritized over raw computational speed.
